idiom_name: hand-written recursive node builder (one malloc per layer, NULL stops)
implementation_notes: C has neither generators nor an unfold combinator, so the anamorphism is written by hand: a function maps a seed to one allocated layer plus the recursive expansion of its children, and both the base case and an allocation failure act as stop conditions. Because the scheme is recursive, structure depth equals stack depth, and deep or input-driven seeds need an explicit worklist with parent links instead of recursion. Ownership is the real design decision: one owner must free the produced structure in a second traversal (or the builder takes an arena from the caller), and when the structure is consumed immediately a callback sink is usually better than returning a container because nothing has to be allocated at all.
pitfalls: Recursion depth equals structure depth: an input-driven seed either overflows the C stack or must be driven by an explicit stack with parent pointers.
malloc failure and the base case are indistinguishable when both return NULL, so the caller cannot tell a truncated structure from a complete one - return a status separately.
The produced structure has no ownership contract: passing it across a module or library boundary without a matching free function leaks or double-frees.
